No 1 is the Coppie of the first blanck sent in the yeare 1606 wth the new Addic̃on now onelie to be deliured to Callicutt or to such Prince as you shall vnderstand, the same was then formrlie deliured

No 2 & 3 is 2 blancke of the Tenor of that to Suratt to any Prince vnto whome formrlie noe łres hath beene sent & therefore wthout the said Addic̃on No 4 is the Gournor of a Cittie of the tenor of that to Aden wthout any Addic̃on for that noe łres hath beene heretofore sent thither, the wch is intended for Moccha some 10 miles from Aden vnder the Comand of the Grandsenior.

No 5 The 5 & last Blancke alsoe to the Gournor of some Cittie of the same tenor of that to Aden wthout any Addic̃on for the reason aforesaid in no: 4 & wthout any nominac̃on of or kinge maties: Amitie wth the grandsenior for that the same is intended for some Cittie out of his Dominions.

Lres of safe Condut 2 for Iohn Iourdan & Phillip Glascocke &c: goeing to the East Indies . 1607

JAMES by the grace of God of greate Brittaine ffraunce and Ireland Kinge Defendor of the faith &c: To all and eury one Kinge, Princes, Duke, Marquesses State Admiralle Captaines Castellers Gournors and Superiors of Provinces Citties Townes Seas Rivers of 1 Bridge &c: & to all other of what order or place soeur haueing Comaund power Magistracie or Iurisdicc̃on health. Such as take vpon them greate matters aboue the vulgar vse and Custome verie proffitable to humane Societie deserue not onelie prayse and favor of all men, but alsoe aide and helpe asmuch as may be lawfullie & convenientlie yealded. In the wch kinde scarce any can be [ ]1 proffitable & worthy then of them, the wch by long Peregrinac̃ons greate [ ] danger of life, veiweing most remote & vnknowne Nac̃ons & kingdomes [ ] Sea doe seeke eury wheare all oportunities of Comodities, & doe [ ]allie a kinde of Societie and Comunicac̃on of Comodities among all [ ]clude doe Contract the vniursitie of Mankinde & the whole world [ ]e Cittie & Communion. And forasmuch as crteine or subiectę [ ] this selfe same minde & intencon take vpon them a Iourney [ ] that wthout the iniury or trouble of any man they may [ ]d Comodious meanes to or subiectę of Interchandge of [ ] people & of mrchandizeing thingę it be most iust and [ ] anitie that vnto the selfe same mrchauntę & vnto their ffactors [ ] and comeing by Sea and land be granted vnto them of all [ ]de, Yet that they may mor safelie and redilie proceede in their [ ]hey may haue the inclinac̃ons of all men of what order & place [ ] the shall come more redy to graunte them that libertie, & to be fauorable [ ] wch by the lawe of humanitie as is said before ought to be granted of [ ] wish the same to be obtenied by or Intercession & for that cause wee [ ]nient to giue theis or łres of safe Conduct & Comendačon to crteine [ ]hauntę of ors and namelie to Iohn Iourdan and Phillipp Glascocke by [ ]ie much intreate all & singuler Kingę Princes Duke Marquesses Admiralls and superiors of Provinces Townes Castles & Portę & all others of what degree and place soeur haueing magistracy Iurisdicčon or power as may be agreeable to the order and dignitie of eury one, that you will geue leaue to the foresaid or subiectę & either of them, or to any other that shall bring theis or łres vnto you by Land or sea to goe or to saile to goe forward or retourne & as their occasion shall requier to remaine in their dominions & that they will not geue or suffer any lett hindrance Iniurie or molestačon to be done vnto them, but that they will yeald vnto them such Offices of benevolence and humanitie as shall be convenient to be yealded to honest men and strangers vndertakeing soe longe and laborious a Iourney: handling their owne affaires & behaueing themselues honestlie & peaceablie. In the wch kinde of Office or any other that may mutuallie be expected of vs we will be most redie to retourne the like favor vnto all & singuler yf occasion shall serue as shall be due to eury one according to their order place & dignitie Giuen out of or Pallace of Westm̄ this xxiiith of ffebruarie 1607.

JAMES REX.

The Coppie of a lre sent to mr Alexander Sharpie Genrall.1
1& of the order of Courte not to deale in any other manner but by way of marchantdize. 11 of March 1607

AFTER my hartie Comendačons &c: According to order of a Courte of the Adventurers in this present 4th voyadge held the fift of this instant Theis are to advertice you that the Companie are pleased and soe doe thinke it fitt that you wth yor Leiuetenante Generall mr Rowles, & such as may happen to succeede you in this voyadge doe make espetiall accompt of Ioseph Salbancke2 aswell in all yor Councells as otherwise, & the rather for that they doe esteeme him to be a man verie sufficient for any place wherein you shall vse him. And further the Companie thinke it meete that you doe carefullie reserue [and]3 keepe this lre amongst other yor Comissions, that you and such as

“Sharpie Genrall signifieing vnto him that the Companie are pleased, and thinke yt “fitt, that he wth the Leiuetenante Genrall and such as shall succeede them doe “make espetiall vse of Ioseph Salbancke in their Councell, & otherwyse vnlesse they “shall finde some iuste reason to the Contrarie. And further willinge him to keepe “and reserue this his lre amongst other his Comissions that he and such as shall “succeede him may take notice thereof, as there shall be occasion.” (Court Minutes, 5th March, 1607/8.) “Att this Courte his maties lres and Comissions wth his maties saffe Conduct, & “their Coppies in English were now deliured to mr Sharpie, wth expresse Admonicon “that they doe their best endevors for the performeing of this voyadge by way of honest “mrchandize, to wch end & purpose onelie we haue sett them forth & furnished them “wthall thinges needfull & necessarie to that effect, wth expresse order alsoe that they “doe abstaine from dealeing wth any person in beraeueing manner, nor in any other “then in freindlie sorte: vnlesse onelie wth such who shall seeke to provoke them “therevnto, by any hindrance to their quiett trade: by taking of any or goodes &c: “According to the Tenor of his mates Comission now by vs procured for them. Aswell “for the avoiedinge of all scandall to the Company as for performance of his mates: “said Comission, as they will awnsweare the Contrarie.” (Ibid., 11th March, 1607/8.) may [happen] to succeede you as aforesaid may take notice thereof from tyme to [tyme as there] shall be occasion. Wherewth I Comitt you all to the Tuition of [Almightie God who] send you a prosperous successe in all yor affaires. London th[ ] [Thomas Smyth]

To or loueing freind mr Willm Kealinge Genrall in or third voyadge to the East Indies, & in his absence to such other of or ffactors as shall be Resident at Bantam or ells where in the said East Indies.1

A Copie of this lre deliured to mr Sharpie Generall for his better vnderstandinge what is on their parte to be done therein.
Twoe copies sent one to mr Kealing & an other to mr Hawkins wth this Superscripcon.

AFTER or hartie Comendañons &c: Since yor depture from or Coaste in Aprill last we haue not heard from you the wch we conceiue to happen by noe default in you, but onelie for that you haue not had any meanes to write vnto vs, & we doubt not but ere this you are all in saffetie arriued to some of or desiered Porte in the Indies accordinge to yor Comission where we hope that by yor good industrie and carriadge we shall finde sufficient & proffitable trade, & likewise haue those retournes wch you shall make home in such Comodities as for their qualitie and goodnes will be more beneficiall vnto vs, then hitherto we haue had as before yor depture hence, & by by yor instruccõns you haue beene sufficientlie informed, & therefore we make noe question but you will doe yor vtmost endevors therein as we put or trust in you.

And resolving the Continuance of or trade in those pte as we haue at yor being heare ympted vnto you, we haue now prepared twoe shipps (viz) the Assencõn & the Vnion of wch shipps and men by Comission from or kinge matie: mr Alexander Sharpie is or Generall in the Assencõn & mr Richard Rowles his Leiuetenante Genrall in the Vnion by whome we haue now sent theis or lres vnto you, and thoughe wee cannot but giue you to vnderstand that this voyadge is solie one ioincte stocke seurall from any of the former voyadge, yett the same is sett forth by some alsoe interessed in the third voyadge, whoe are authorized & allowed by the genrall Companie to doe the same And are inclined & authorized the next yeare to doe the like. Wherefore as the forenamed Generall and others now sent haue order for their pte to doe the best Assistaunce they cann, soe we wish you to shew them all kindnes and favor you may, aswell in the direccõn of their trade & saffetie as otherwise, yett soe as the Accompte be noe way mingled, nor the proceedinge of either, be any way preiudiceall thone to thother & they Comeing to any place wherein you shall be Resident as loueing Brothers and servante of one Companie you are to instruct them by the best meanes you may howe you haue there proceeded wth the Superiors of the place, & what you haue done concrninge the setlinge of yor trade, & howe the same is likelie to stand. And alsoe of what els shall be fitt for the Comon good, that you wth them & they wth you may soe agree in Concorde that all thinge may be soe done as both you and we may haue comforte of yor proceedinge therein.

And forasmuch as that or men the wch you shall leaue in those pte may haue some occasion of longer staie theare before retourne of or shipps from hence thither vnto them againe, then we at yor being heare intended: we wish you to giue them expresse chardge soe to carie them selues that they may be esteemed good husbande for the Companie, rather increasers then diminishers of what stocke you shall leaue wth them. And it is expected that by their good industrie in buieing of Cashes & other ymploimentę they may easilie beare their chardges theare, wth ourplus to the proffitt of the Companie wch as is reported they bring to their owne priuate the wch we cannot endure And well pvsing our or łres by you sent vnto them doe vse their best endevors to applie them selues diligentlie to pforme or direcc̃ons therein mencioned, & what els, by experience they may learne, that when or shipps shall come thither both we & the may finde them to haue beene both diligent industrious & good and faithfull Stewardę to the Companie, & for better pformance of or said direcc̃ons, we haue now sent them a Coppie of or foresaid łres by you mr Kealinge sent the last yeare. And further theis are to requier you that if the shipps of the Adventurers in the 4th voyadge shall happen to come where you shall be resident & wante ladeing of their owne. That then & in such case you haueing any goodę to send home you doe lade soe much of the best thereof as convenientlie they shall be able to take in, being it much better that the same be soe brought home then that it should lie theare dead: wherein you are to haue due care that the Accomptę of either pte be noe way mingled & that yor goodę sent doe come vnder a seurall Marke, Consigned by Bills of ladinge to the vse of the Gournor and Companie of the Adventurers in the third voyadge, takeing the best order that you can for keepinge of the seurall goodę of both voyadgę apte thone from thother & that łres be writte what shall be remaineinge for each Accompt. And further you shall vnderstand That if by theis meanes you shall send home any of or goodę by the said shipps of the Adventurers in the 4th voyadge & for the same or for some other cause there shall be noe need or ymployment for soe many of or ffactors there wch may happen to be left. Then we doe order that some of the most insufficientest of or ffactors there be brought home by the said shipps in the 4th voyadge if in the discrec̃on of the now Generall mr Sharpie & the cheeffest of or ffactors there it shall be soe thought fitt. And alsoe if the Adventurers in the said 4th voyadge shall leaue any ffactors in the Indies where you shall be resident, That the ffactors in both the voyadgę doe remaine and liue together At the chardge equallie p rato accordinge to the quantitie of the goodę wch shall be there left for each accompt And thus not doubting of yor faithfull care and diligence in the premisses we pray God to blesse you all London the 12th day of March 1607.

Yor loueing ffreinde the Gournor Comitties & Generalitie of the Companie of mrchante trading into the East Indies.

This 2 is the draught of the Bill of Aduenture Ph: Graeff urget (?) to haue.

TO ALL1 to whome this present writing shall come to be seene herd or red wee the gouernor and Companie of Marchaunte of London trading into the Easte Indians send greeting in our Lord god everlasting Whereas wee the said Gouernor and Companie of Marchaunte haue Entertayned Phillip de Grauæ3 of the precinct of St Katherins neare the Tower of London Marrioner to goe as principall mr for or vses in this p̄nte voyadge nowe by vs prepared towardes the saide Easte Indians Knowe yee therefore that wee the saide Gouernor and Companie of Marchaunte for the further allowance and recompence of the good service trauell and paines wch hee the said Phillip de Grauæ intendeth to p̄forme in the said voyage doe by these p̄nte for or selues and everie of vs and the Executors and adm̄strators of vs and everie of vs Covenante promise and graunte to and wth the said Phillip de Grauæ his executors adm̄strators and assignes, To give pay and allowe vnto him the saide Phillip de Grauæ his executors adm̄strators or assignes oute of or proper stockes aduentured in the said voyadge wthin six Monethes next after that the said shippes wch is now bounde of the saide voyadge to the East Indians or any of them shall returne into the River of Thames neighe the port of London and all the goode laide on land in London The benifitt proffitt and gaine that shall growe of ffive hundred and ffiftie poundes sterling (according to the rate of such an adventure in the said voyadge) oute of the gaine wch god shall send by the returne of the said voyage, (The Charges of the voyadge & of the goode returned therevppon groweing dew to be paied being ffirste deducted) In wittnes whereof wee haue herevnto Caused or Common Seale to be put and deliuered this as or deede yeeven the day of 1607 Annoq RRis: Iacobi Anglie &ca quinto Et Scotie quadragesimo primo.

IN the name of God Amen the last of Februarie 1607.

A Comission1 set downe by vs the Gournor Deputie and Comitties of the mrchaunte of London trading to the East Indies for better direcc̃on of or loueing freinde the Generall Leuietenante & other the Captaines mrchante Masters & Mariners in this or intended fourth voyadge to those pte wch we humblie beseech god to blesse wth a happie Conclusion.

I 2 ships prepared & mr Sharpie appointed Genrall

Inprimis whereas we the mrchaunte aforesaid haue prepared wth or greate chardge & trouble Twoe Shipps (viz) the Assenc̃on of 350 Tonns Phillipp de Graeffe mr, And the Vnion of 400 Tonns Griffin Morris2 mr, for a voyadge by Gode grace by them to be made to the East Indies, & haue furnished them sufficientlie, & in plentifull manner wth men Tackle victualls & all other needfull prouisions fitt for such a voyadge: of a spetiall trust and Confidence wch we haue in the integritie & iust carrieinge of or loueinge freind Alexander Sharpie we doe appointe and authorize him Genrall to goe in the Assenc̃on and to Comand or said shipps & all the men in them haueing procured him sufficient authoritie from or souereigne Lord the kinge matie: for that purpose not doubtinge but that he will soe behaue himselfe as he may be both feared and loued & that he will wth all his diligence and endevor prosecute or designes and labor to bringe this or intended voyadge to a happie end.

The Leiuetenante Generall. 2

Item we appointe and ordeine or loueing freind Richard Rowles to be Leiuetenante of or said shipps & men and to take his passadge in the Vnion, wch Comanders ffactors mrs: & Mariners we trust will soe carrie them selues wth such due respect one to an other, and obedience to eury one of their Superiors as loue & kindnes be contynued on all side, & all whollie applie their witte & endevors for the due pformance of this voyadge, in the best manner they may for the good of the Companie.

ffor religious gournmt & prayers dailie 3

Item and for that religious gournmt & exercise doth best binde men to pforme their duties it is principallie to be cared for that prayers be said morninge and eveninge in each shipp and the whole Companie called therevnto, wth diligent Eyes that none be wantinge that all ioinctlie may wth reuerence and humilitie pray vnto Almightie god to blesse and preserue them from all danger in this longe and tedious voyadge.

Against blasphemeinge & vnlawfull games. 4

Item that noe blasphemeing of god, swearing thefte dronkennes or otherlike disorders be vsed but that the same be sevearelie ponished, & that noe diceinge or other vnlawfull games be admitted for that most comonlie the same is the begynninge of quarrellinge and many tymes murther a iust occasion of Gode wrath and vengeance from wch the Lord deliur vs. Therefore it shall be needfull that such orders be sett vp and published in each shipp and such punishmt appointed for such offence as may giue notice to eury man what he ought to avoied.

To abstaine from shedding liquor in the Ballast & for keeping the shipps cleane 5

Item that spetiall order be geven that noe liquor be spilt in the ballast of the shipps, or filthines be left wthin bourd, wch in heate breadeth noysome smells & infecc̃on but that there be a diligent care to keepe the ourlopps & other places of the shipps cleane and sweete wch is a notable preservac̃on of health, wherein the Dutchmen doe farr exceede vs in cleanlines to their greate Comendac̃ons & disgrace to or People.

ffor keepinge Iournalls. 6

Item that Continuall and true Iournalls be kept of eury daies Course & Nauigac̃on during the whole voyadge wth a true relac̃on of eury thinge, that passeth & this not onelie to be done by the seurall Captaines, mrs, Pilatte & mrs mate but alsoe by the mrchaunte and Pursars, & that some of the principalls in each shipp may Conferr together at convenient tymes, when the Generall shall call them, therevnto, to thend that if any haue forgotten what an other obserued, the same may be added soe as a pfect discourse may be sett downe, to be presented to the Gournor and Companie when god shall grante them a saffe retourne, to be kept for better direcc̃on of posteritie.

ffor keepinge Companie at Sea. 7

Item that the Generall & mr of his shipp doe sett downe & deliur such instrucc̃ons to the Comanders of thother shipp that they may keepe Companie together for the better releife and Comforte one of an other, And if separac̃on of them should happen by Constrainte of weather or Tempest that they should agree vpon a course before hand, & of a place whither to applie their selues to finde each other.

To settle the seurall provisions in each mans chardge after they shall come to Sea & to deliur nothinge out wthout warrant for wch they are to be awnswerable vpon their wages. 8

Item that the Genrall Leiertenante & mrs of the shipps take due notice by Inventory from eury Officer of the shipps before they depte out of the Thames of the seurall provisions deliured to each shipp & soe sone as they shall come to Sea & not before to settle the same in the chardge of the Officers appointed for that purpose in either shipp vntill wch tyme all stores are to remaine vnder locke and key and that the same be entred in the Pursars Booke vnder written by the said Officers, to thend that such thinge as are provided for their needfull supplies may not be ymbecilled, & that nothinge thereof of any value be ymployed for any vse whatsoeur wthout a warrante vnder the hand of the Generall directed to the Officer that hath such chardge, wch warrante shall serue for their dischardge in their Accomptę, otherwise to be awnswearable for the same wth their wage, & eury such warrant to be registred in the Pursars Booke the day of the monneth & the occasion & this vpon forfecture of soe much out of the Pursars wage, this order to be obserued alsoe in each of the shipps by the Comanders mrs Pursars & Officers as aforesaid, that at the retourne of the said shipps a true Accompt may be yealded howe and in what mannr the same haue beene vsed & ymployed.

Not to straggle 9

And whereas the stragling of yor men in any place where they shall arriue or come may proue not onelie the losse of such as shall soe straggle although they shall be Armed, but alsoe thereby much hurte may happen to the Residue of or People & generallie to the whole Companie. Yt is ordered that you doe not ꝑmitt any man in any place where you shall come (vpon what ground soeur) to straggle or goe from the Residue of yor Companies vnlesse they be by you first warranted therevnto, & that vpon iust occasion, vpon paine of seveare ponishment to be inflicted of such as shall doe the Contrarie still doubtinge the worst and standinge vpon yor guarde night and day in eury place where you shall come wthout yealdinge any trust to those People.

what is to be obserued at wateringe 10.

Item we Comend vnto you the Generall principallie & to the rest of the Comanders and mrs: an espetiall care that at eury place where you shall water and refresh yor men you call the Companies together geueing them seveare warninge to behaue them selues peaceablie and Ciuillie towarde the People of that place the better to pcure their freindshipp towarde the supplie of yor wante, & the like in eury place wheare you come, least the losse of yor liues & ourthrowe of or voyadge pay for yor disorders, beside an vtter discreditt to or Nacõn, and that yor men doe vse a discreete meane in eatinge of fruite and fresh victualls least the surfett & fall into diseases, whereof we haue had too much experience. And the better to refraine vnrulie appetite we hould it Convenient that the Generall appointe some of the discreetest in the Companies to procure & prouide in such places what you wante, and the same being prouided and brought to the Generall, by him to be repted1 to each Companie what may be needfull, and that none presume to doe the Contrarie wthout seueare ponishmt, And that a spetiall care be had to releeue the sicke wth such fresh meatę & other Comfortable thingę wherewth we haue furnished each shipp for that purpose, & not otherwyse to be spent in Royott and bankettinge, & soe the sicke pꝛishe for wante of thingę needfull: Yet or expresse order is that you neur putt into any Harbor wthout greate occasion, & then vpon crteine knowledge of the Securitie of the place and vigilent care night and day to prevent Dangers takeing espetiall notice from place to place of the Course of the Monsomes for yor better direcõns if you shall haue occasion to goe to diurs places.

To water at St: Lawrence, & sett vp their Pinnasse & followe Sr Iames Lancaster’s direccons 11.

Item for the fittest place of refreshinge we wish you to shape yor Course to the Porte of St Augustine in the Iland of St Lawrence, where you shall finde good Harbor & plentie of victualls, in wch place it will not be fitt to make longe aboade but make hast and endevor to be vpon the Coaste of Melinde in the monneth of Iulie at the ffurthest, but for yor better direcõn therein we referr you to the instruccõns of Sr Iames Lancaster1 now deliured you herewth, whoe can best direct you for yor course vpon that Coaste by his owne experience, except you in yor discrecõns finde otherwyse more fitt: still standinge vpon yor guarde in eury place wthout yealding any trust to those People. At wch place alsoe we hould it fitt, & tyme will then best serue to that effect, that you settogether and make readie yor Pinnace the wch you carrie wth you, & alsoe you may heare informe yor selues if or shipps & men sent the last yeare haue beene theare, when, & wch way they tooke &c: for better direcõn of the Busines you are now sent aboute as occasion shall serue.

Beware of the fflattes of the coast of Melinde, & what they are to buie & obserue. 12

ITEM after yor depture from the Porte of St Augustine towardę the Coast of Melynde beware of the fflattę of Iudea2 wch lie betweene the Iland of St Lawrence & the firme land: vpon wch fflattę it is said that the Currantę doe sett. There is alsoe an Iland vpon the Coaste of Melinde verie fitt for refreshinge yor people as we are informed & whereof the Hollenders had experience in their last voyadge that way: The wch Iland is called Zinzabar where if you finde it needfull & haue tyme for that purpose you may theare water and refresh yor Companies, els not. And alsoe it shall not be amisse as you saile alonge wthout staye in any place or goeinge a shoare to buie some Oliphauntę Teeth wch are bought at Mozambique & on the Coaste of Melinde in greate abondance, and carried into the Indies. That Commoditie is exceedinglie requested in Cambaia alsoe stoare of Ambergreece is likewise to be had in the Coaste of Melinde and at St Lawrence Iland: But goe not either to Mozambique nor to the Iland of Pemba in any hand but leaue it on yor larborside.

To make diligent inquirie of all thinges needfull 13

It is further ordered that all the way alonge as you saile, or wheare you shall come you doe yor best endevor to vnderstand what good saffe Harbors are in each place to be had for vs to trust vnto, for maintenance of a Trade in those pte in saffetie from danger of Portugalls or others: vnder whome in each place the People are in subiection: & of what nature they are: what havens they be, of what condicõn & vnder whose Comand, together wth the dangers & depthes of waters in each place for passadge what trade may be thear had, the sorte prices and goodnes of Comodities, as alsoe what sorte of ors are there best requested as likewyse by what speedie meanes you may send or bringe vs tres ourland of what shall be fitt for vs to haue knowledge of by way of Turkie or otherwise, and for yor better saffetie in yor passadge therein (if need be) we haue ꝑcured you his maties: saffe Conduct1 the wch we haue geven to you the Generall to be deliured to such as shall be vsed in this respect, endevoring as Convenientlie you may wthout any ympedimt to yor voyadge findinge thingę proffitable, to vse the best meanes to drawe the people vnto you in their Iunckę or Boatę wth some of their mrchandize for wch you may assay to barter some of or owne, or sell and buie as you shall see occasion: As alsoe endevoringe to doe & vnderstand what ells shall be for the Comon good of the Companie, & for future experience.

Some order to be sett downe touching dead mens goodes 14.

ITEM it is expresslie ordered that by a Generall Consent, of you the Generall Captaine ffactorrs Masters & Mariners some good order be by you taken & sett downe in writeinge soe soone as you come to Sea, concrninge the disposeing of dead mens goode in the voyadge, by sale at the Maste, or otherwise for buieinge sellinge borrowinge & lendinge one an other, & ordering what sallarie shall be allowed the Pursars vpon eury pound for keepinge Accompt thereof to avoied Controursie and Question hereafter, & eury Mariner and other of each shipp to sett their hand or marke vnto the same order. But if any ffactor shall happen to die his goode, Booke, Accompte, & other thinge are to be by order of the Generall and Leiuetenant Generall saffelie reserued & brought home for England.

ffor better prservacon of health by washing Caske 15.
ffor inquirie for the Suzan. 16.

Item for better preseruac̃on of health or order is that from tyme to tyme as the water Caske shall be emptied of fresh water it be forthwth againe filled wth salt water for preven c̃on of leakeinge and Mustines Item or direc̃con is that you make diligent inquirie at St Lawrence & Zinzabar, & all other places in yor passadge and retourne of Tydinge of the Suzan:1 or if any English shipp hath beene of late wthin theis two yeares either cast away or taken, or putt in for reliefe in any of those pte & receiueing any knowledge of her to vse the best meanes you may for recoury of her, her men, and goode, Soe as it may be noe way priudicious to yor proceedinge in yor voyadge.

To go thence for Zocatora & soe to Aden & Moccha comeinge in tyme els not & what they are to do theare 17.

Item haueing refreshed yor People wthall speede you are to shape yor course for Zocotora nere the mouth of the Red Sea, where is alsoe good refreshinge & (as is said) the best Alloes Sacatrina in the world & likewise stoare of Amber greece, & other thinge whereof we pray you to take notice, & buie thereof, what you shall see convenient but still in all yor mrchandizeing, be carefull to putt of yor English Comodities in Trucke. In this Iland we doubt not but you may be furnished both wth Pilotte for Aden: Or if the same be not fitt for trade by reason as it is reported vnto vs the same is a Garrison Towne rather of Souldiers then Marchaunte.1 Then you are to goe for Moccha a Towne 10 miles from Aden said to be a place of speciall trade right ouer against wch Towne there is an Iland called Kedgee where is alsoe reported to be good Harbor and wateringe (if need shall soe requier) and vnderstandinge what trade there is to be had, what the People be and of what interteinmt: toward strangers, whereof informe yor selues in the best manner you may, as alsoe if or shipps and men sent thither the last yeare haue been at Aden, or theare aboute, & beinge theare what they haue done, and soe findinge of trade and interteinmt wthall convenient speede you are to direct yor course for Aden or Moccha or some other place theareaboute wch you may learne to be more fitter for trade and interteynmt, Soe alwaies Provided you come thither about the fine of Iulie, or in such tyme (if need be) as you may goe thence wth that Monsone for Surate or Bantam, the wch we conceiue you may verie well pforme yf (you findinge not thinge there to yor likeinge,) you make noe staye theare but wthall speede depte thence for Surate by the 20th of September at the furthest the wch you are in any case to doe ells you shall loose the oportunitie of that Monsone, where vnto you are both in goeing and retourninge to haue an espetiall care. And beinge arriued neare the place, come to an Ancor but take heed in any Case you come not wthin their danger, still expecting and feareing evill though there be noe cause.

And comeing thither first you are to vse meanes (if any of or People be theare[])to deliur or lres1 by you sent accordinge to the direccon to mr Willm Hawkins or to the cheefe of or men wch shall be theare lefte, & therevpon to Conferr together wth them and vnderstand what they haue done aboute the deliury of or kinge mate lres sent by them to the Gournor of that place wth a Present as alsoe for their quiett trade &c: That you may the better pceede wth good aduice to doe accordinglie, aswell for deliury of his maties lres now sent by you to the Gournor of Aden or Moccha wth some Convenient present as otherwise as theare shall be occasion, and wthall you are to signifie vnto such of or men as you shall finde there that this fowerthe voyadge is solie one ioincte stocke seuerall from the former Voyadge yet sett out by some of the same Companie authorized and allowed therevnto by the rest accordinge to the Tenor of the same lre now by vs sent vnto them, & accordinglie throughout all the whole voyadge you are to keepe Accompt of the same as a ioincte stocke of it selfe, sett out by vs seurallie from all the former voyadge for those pte. And further if thinge soe stand there as it shall be needfull, you may make it knowne to the Gournor of the place as we haue formrlie geven order to or men to doe (that is) that you are English mrchaunte & haue brought tres vnto him from or kinge matie: seekeinge onlie peaceable trade, aswell for saile of or Comodities as for buieinge of theirs. And therewthall to deliur the same tres wth such present as you shall thinke fitt to the said Gournor wth whome (as you shall see cause) you may treate for Priuiledge and freedome of trade for as many Yeares as you can, if it be not by or men formrlie done or needfull to be enlardged declaringe that or kinge is in League wth the Grandsignior That or People doe trade into Cairo, Aleppo, Damasko, Constantinople, & in all other his Dominions freelie and that or kinge hath now a lidger Imbaffador in Constantinople, wch loue of the Grand Signior towarde or Nacõn, hath ymbouldened vs to visitt that place wth or shipps and goode now desieringe by his favorable lycence to trade as Ciuill & peaceable mrchante & that you desier to settle a ffactorie theare, yf by his honorable favor you may be pmitted, assureing him that by or trade his Customes will be greatelie increased for that we shall endevor to fetch that from thence wch we now fetch from the Molloccos Bantam & diurs other places in the Indies. To wch if he Yeald it shall be needfull that you craue such articles of Priuiledge from him in writeinge for or Nacõn the better to incurradge vs to frequent that place. And for yor better direccon we haue deliured you the Coppie of Priuiledge procured for vs by Sr Iames Lancaster from the Kinge of Achen, addinge therevnto what other thinge shall be needfull. And further if you shall see cause you may make the Gournor acquainted wth what sorte of English Comodities you haue now brought thither, but not (yf it may be) wth any of yor moneys vntill yor Comodities be first sould, at wch place we choose rather to be, then to make triall of any other if possiblie we may.

ffor better sale of or Comodities & buieinge of theirs at Aden.

Item arriueinge at Aden or Moccha & findinge good hope of interteynement & trade whereby either presentlie or in some shorte space by the retourne of their Iouncke from Cambaia you may vent or English Comodities, & finde fitt and sufficient ladeinge there for retournes, we wish you that in the buieinge thereof that you be verie carefull to make choise of that wch is good and fitt for sale, & in sale of or Comodities that you stand vpon the value & estimaçon thereof, Yet soe as you loose not the oportunitie of the first mrkette & reasonable offers least by often veiwinge them they fall to dislike, for Nouelties as you knowe drawe men to buie: and note that by the repaier of all sorte of People thither you shall finde meanes to sell what Comodities of ors are in any place requested yf you putt yor selues forward, & by helpe of some Brokers you seeke to deale: But you must be carefull to vse all men wth kindnes and Ciuillitie, and see that yor men doe the like in any wise, least disorders and scandalous behauior cause you to be abhorred and evill intreated. At wch place as we esteeme it to be the most saffest nearest and cheeffest place for trade we desier rather to be, then at any other, if we may there soe finde proffitable and sufficient trade in saffetie as aforesaid.

ffor Adverticement ourland if need be & by what meanes. 19.

Item if you finde theare that any of or Comodities or Colors will sell better then those we now send, or some of those more vendible then the rest we desier to be adverticed ourland by some Moores that goe to Argier Aleppo or Alexandria and direct yor łres to Richard Allen Consull at Argier to be sent hither wth speede, or to Aleppo to mr Paule Pyndar1 Consull or to 2at Alexandria or any other English men that be there obserueing the note of a Caracter wch we deliur you herewth for better secrecie And not to be backward or slacke by eury Conveyaunce to write least some łres miscarrieinge others may come to hand.

Haueing procured yor lading at Aden to retourne for England. 20
noe ffactors names put into theis spaces left.

And haueinge procured the dispatch of or shipps wth their full ladeinge our direccon is that you retourne for England wth the next fitt winde and weather leaueing there for factors if you thinke needfull2 and such others as you thinke meete wth some convenient allowance & likewise wth order to ymploye their endevors for findinge out of further trade aswell for all sorts of Cloth and Kersies and Colors best requested, as all other of or Comodities and for the buieing of all those Countrie wares obserueing still good and crteine note of all sorte of Comodities brought hither from out of the East Indies: But if after yor arriuall to Aden or Moccha you shall happen not to finde sufficient meanes theare to relade home both yor shipps (as at first you expected) but onelie one of them, nor any hope of further trade there likelie in any good tyme to be made, then or will is you should wth all expedic̃on send home one of yor shipps soe laden for

England vnder the Comand of or Leiuetenante Genrall & thother to goe forward for Cambaia or Bantam as the tyme shall be fitt therevnto, & there shall be convenient stocke to doe the same. Betweene wch place at the mouth of the Red Sea & Cambaia & in the River Syndus as we are informed there is noe doubt of Ample and beneficiall trade in saffetie yf you make diligent search and inquirie for the same wherein we pray you to haue espetiall care. And for yor better pceedinge therein wth any Prince or Gournor you may finde vnto whome you haue not łres alreadie directed vnto them from or kinge matie: we haue pcured you łres from his matie: wth genrall termes in the inside & wth Blancke on the outside to be by you directed to any such Prince or Gournor if you shall happen to haue occasion: But before yor depture one from annother the Leiuetenante Generall is to call vnto you the Generall for the duplicate of his maties: Comission vnder the broad Seale for better Gournment of his men homewarde.

Comeing not to Zocotora in due tyme to goe for Aden, to leaue Aden, & goe directlie for Cambaia & there to followe this & the next ensueing orders.

But yf it shall soe happen you come not to Zocotora in such due tyme as you may convenientlie goe to Aden & haue that Monsone to bringe you into the Indies (if need be) doe not then at any hand goe to Aden or Moccha but saile directlie towarde Surate the entrance of Cambaia, where if you come aboute the middle of September you shall finde it Somer and faier weather soe as you may saffelie ride in the open Roade. But if the same place shall not be found fitt for trade according to or expectac̃on by reason of some dangers that may happen vnto you by the Portugalls of Diu and Demon1 whoe as is said haue the Comand of those Seas & receiue tribute of the People of those place, Then you are to saile for Lawrie2 in the Bay of the River Syndus. aboute 2 daies saileing from Surate, where, as we are informed is good Harbor in saffetie wthin 2 miles of wch Towne vp in that Bay there is a greate Cittie as bigg as London called Negertuttie,1 where is plentie of Indico Callicoes & diurs other mrchandizes fitt for England the people whereof are free, onelie gourned by the kinge of 2 Arcabar whoe recideth at Agree some fortie English Miles from Negertuttie, at wch place the Portugalls haue nothinge to doe, but onelie come thither for mrchandize, as other strangers, where it is conceyued if you behaue yor selues well and gentlie towarde those people you will finde ample and proffitable trade aswell of their Comodities as for vent of or Comodities theare, where it is reported Clothes of all sorte is in great request. At wch place or places if vpon diligent inquirie you shall finde a crteine and saffe expectac̃on of trade & that or shipps may goe into saffe Harbors free from danger of the Portugalls or any other: Then you are to staye in the open Roade neare the Barr of Cambaia or at Lawrie & by some of the People wch come out eury Tyde from thence, or otherwise we wish you to doe yor best endevors to vnderstand yf or shipps and men sent for those pte the last yeare, haue beene there, & being there what they haue done, & soe findinge hope of saffetie & interteinment to send word to some of or men (yf any shall be there) that you are arriued wishing to haue Conference wth them before you make yor comeing knowne to the Gournor of that place aswell concrninge what they haue done in the deliury of or kinge maties: łres by them sent to the kinge of Cambaia & Present as otherwise of what hope of interteinmt & quiett trade may be there expected that therevpon you may proceed wth good advice to doe accordinglie for deliury of or kinge maties: łres & Present now alsoe by you sent to the kinge of Cambaia as for the obtayneinge of quiett trade & otherwise as there shall be occasion. And comeinge thither & findinge some of or men theare you are to deliur or łres now sent vnto them accordinge to the direcčõn, & to signifie vnto them that this voyadge is solie one ioinct stocke seurall from the former voyadge, and yett sett out by some of the same Company authorized and allowed therevnto by the rest, accordinge to the Tenor of the same łre from vs vnto them,1 & accordingelie through out all the whole voyadge you are to keepe Accompt of the same as of a ioincte stocke of it selfe by vs sett out seurall from all the formr voyadge as is before specified in the 17 Article.

22

But if none of or men be theare, & notwthstanding there be vpon informačõn good hope of quiett trade, & kinde interteinemt in saffetie. Then at your arriuall as aforesaid you are neurthelesse to send word to the Gournors or Comanders there that there is a Messenger arriued wth łres from the kinge matie: of England vnto their kinge praying the Gournors to send them a boate wth saffe Conveyaunce. And if any come to you from the Gournors Then we thinke it fitt that you the Generall doe repaier thither takeing wth you his maties: łres & Presente & such other provisions as you haue for that purpose, & in yor Companie take wth you twoe of or ffactors Reaue1 and Iourdan & yor owne servant whoe are barrelled to that effect or whome els you shall finde most meete for that purpose, & comeinge to the Gournor of Surate or Lawrie present him wth some guifte what you shall thinke meete, & desier them to assist you wth meanes and guide to their kinge that you may deliur his mate said łres & present vnto that kinge craue a speedie awnsweare and his maties: resolučõn if he will be pleased or not to grante you free and saffe trade in his Countries and Harbors accordinge to the Tenor of his mate: said łre wth sufficient defence against those that shall practise to ympeach or hinder the same, or annoy or hurte any of the shipps Bodies or goode of any of or Nac̃on. And the better to induce the kinge to grante vs Priviledge and free trade signifie that we will be readie to bringe him Armor and other munic̃on from tyme to tyme in or seurall voyadge for the better inablinge him against his Enimyes beside the increase of his Customes wch will be greater for that thereby we shall fetch that from thence wch we now fetch from the Molloccos Bantam and diurs other places in the Indies, & that you seeke onelie peaceable trade aswell for buieinge of their Comodities as for sale of yor owne, wch if he promyse to doe, then desier to haue Comissioners appointed to Consider wth you of Articles in writeinge for setlinge of a ffactorie (yf need be) & for Priuiledge of Trade for as many yeares as you can procure to be granted to or Nac̃on the better to incourradge vs to frequent his kingdomes yf the same be not formrlie ꝑcured by or men not1 needfull further to be inlardged. And for yor better direcc̃on therein, we haue deliured you the foresaid Coppie of the Priviledge formrlie procured for vs by Sr: Iames Lancaster from the kinge of Achen,2 addinge thervnto what other thinge shall be needfull: wch Priviledge beinge obtayned and signed by the kinge, haueinge taken yor leaue in Comelie manner, and receiued such Comoonde-mte in writeinge directed to his Gournors and Officers of his Townes and Porte, as you can pcure for yor defence against all disturbers of you in yor peaceable trade. And for their Assistance of you & kinde interteinmt in the same, you are wthall speede to make yor retourne to Surate or to Lawrie aforemencioned: And haueing deliured that kinge Comandement to the Gournor and Officers there craue their Assistance wth Pilotte & saffe Conducc̃on of yor shipps & therewth make all the expedic̃on you can to gett into the Harbor: But first shewe to some trustie Brokers, paterns of such yor Clothes kersies and other Comodities as are in or shipps, whereof, as of such moneys we haue nowe sent you haue3 an Invoice, takeinge knowledge wch sorte of those Comodities wilbe theare best sold & accordinglie giue order for fetching of them a shoare in saffe manner. And further if you shall see cause you make the Gournors acquainted wth what sorte of English Comodities you haue now brought thither but not (yf otherwise possiblie) wth any of yor moneys vntill yor Comodities be first sold.

ffindinge vent att Cambaia for or commodities & fitt retourne of theirs for England what the are to doe for sale & buieinge thereof. 23.

And findinge that you may vent or English Comodities & finde pffitable and sufficient ladinge there for retournes as Indico, Cotton yarne fine Callicoes Opium Gumlacre Beniamyn Muske Sivitt Amber Mirr, Olibinum, pretious stones Bezars &c: we wish you that in the buieinge thereof you be verie carefull to make choise of that wch is good & fitt for sale, & in sale of or Comodities that you stand vpon the value and estimacõn thereof as in the 18th Article.

Haueing procured ye ladeinge of their ships at Cambaia to retourne home and leaue ffactors. 24

And haueing procured the dispatch of or shipps wth their full ladeinge at Surate or Lawrie or theareaboute of some proffitable Comodities as aforesaid the most ptę whereof to be Indico you are to retourne for England wth the next fitt wynde and weather leaueing there for ffactorrs (if you shall thinke needfull)1

And such others as you shall appointe wth some convenient allowance, & likewise wth order to ymploy all their endevors for findinge out of further trade aswell for all sorte of Clothes & kersies as their Colors best requested as all other of or Comodities, & for the buieinge of those Countrie wares obserueinge still good & crteine note of all sorte of Comodities there to be sould as is formrlie mencioned in the 20th Article. Wheare alsoe before yor retourne for England you are accordinge to yor direcc̃on in the 17th article to take the best informac̃on you can of the state of Aden, as what Harbors and Pilotte to bringe men in, are theare to be had what Condic̃on the People are of what trade & what interteinemt towarde strangers, what thinge will be there vendible & saleable &c: & what els shall be needfull to be knowne in that respect, & to acquainte vs therewth for or better knowledge what to doe if hereafter at any tyme we shall thinke good to visitt that place.

findinge ladinge but for one shipp to send her home by the Leiuetenante Genrall & the duplicate of
his mates Comission & send the other for Bantam haueinge but 2000li stocke to relade her thence. 25.

But if after yor arriuall to Surate or Lawrie or theareaboute you shall happen not to finde fitt and sufficient ladinge theare to relade home both yor shipps as you first expected but onelie one of them, nor any hope of ffurther trade there likelie in any reasonable tyme to be made, then or will is if you haue but left of or stocke sent wth you to the some of 2000li in moneys or in such Pinthadoes or Callicoes as you shall there puide for Bantam & the Molloccos you shall wthall expedicõn send home for England, one of yor said shipps soe laden vnder the Comand of or Leiuetenante Generall whoe before his depture from you is to call vnto you the Generall for the duplicate of his mate: Comission vnder the Broade seale for the gournmt of his men homewarde as aforesaid and the other shipp wthall expedicõn to goe directlie thence for Bantam for better pformance whereof, you are soe to order yor affaires at Surate, That you may be suer (if need be) you may haue the Monsone to bringe you thither.

If all the stock nowe sent will fullie lade both the shipps then it is to be putt in both & retourned for England. 26

But if at yor being at Surate or Lawrie or theareaboute you shall haue occasion by the Costlines of the Comodities you shall theare puide to ymploy all or stocke of moneys & Comodities you shall now carrie wth you, for such proffitable Comodities of those place as is before mencioned, & the same will not be sufficient fullie to relade both the shipps home, Then or will is you lade the same Comodities so bought in both the shipps equallie accordinge to their Bourthen & retourne wth all expedicõn directlie for England leaueing there some ffactors wth Convenient allowance yf you shall thinke meete as aforesaid.

But findinge not trade at Cambaia to goe directlie for Bantam, & what is there ordered to be done. 27

But yf at Surate or Lawrie or theareaboute you be not kindlie dealt wthall nor cannott by any meanes finde interteinmt in saffetie or sufficient Comõditie to relade one or both of yor shipps home. Then you are wth both the shipps and Pinnace to shape yor course alonge the Coaste of Mallabar wth that Monsone for Bantam wth such Pinthadoes and Callicoes as you can gett for those place where you haueinge deliured our tres accordinge to the direccõn of or ffactors at Bantam & made them acquainted that what we now send is a ioincte stocke seurallie of it selfe, accordinge to the Tenor of or said tre as before is mencioned in the 121 & 17 Articles we referr you to Consider wth them theare what is best to be done wherein vsinge such direcc̃ons for yor reladeinge homewardę as you shall be then best advised: either wth Mace Nutmegge & Cloues at the Mollocos, or wth the same and Pepp. Wherein alsoe you are to remember and foresee that in ladeing those Comodities you buie such as are drie & not greene, & that you cleanse them what you can that the ships be not stuffed wth such vnproffitable ware as is not worth the Custome, wherein we pray you to omitt noe tyme.

See you haue yor weight & the Bagges nombred & mrked. 28

Item be verie carefull that you haue yor due weight & the same putt into Bagge nombred and mrked & sent abourd the shipps wth some of the ffactors or some other trustie p̄sons wth a note conteyneinge the p̄ticuler of eury Bagge vnder the nomber, the same note to be deliured to the Pursar whome we chardge to weigh eury Bagg at the takeing of it into the shipp, wherby he may see that the weight is accordinge to the note receiued, keepinge eury note & entringe the Contente into his booke, whereby yf any error happen it may be found out wch we wish you the Generall to examine eury night that there growe noe abuse.

ffor sale of victuall & Canvesse &c: 29.

Item forasmuch as in former voyadge soe now in this theare may be occasion for the benefitt of the Companie to make sale of some of yor Victualls Canvesse or some other thinge belonging to yor stoare, or otherwise whereof you shall happen to haue noe neede. Yt is therefore ordered that good care be had that the same be done not onlie for the proffitt of the Companie wthout any danger to the voyadge: But alsoe brought (as all other thinge) to the genrall Accompt of the Companie.

The Pursars chardge for keepeing a true accompt of all thinges brought in & caried out of the shipps 30.

Item we chardge that the Pursar be continuallie abourd the shipp and take true notice of all thinge, whatsoeur are brought into the shipp or carried out, either by the Genrall Captaines, mrs: Mariners the Pursar himselfe, or whosoeur the same to be entred into his Booke vnder the name of the owner that eury one may haue his due at the retourne as the Pursar will awnsweare it wth the losse of his wage and we pray the Generall and Captaines to geue the Pursar strict order for p̄formance thereof.

One hatch onelie open at the ladinge of the shipps & leaueing worke to lock it &c: 31

Item that there be but one hatch open (yf it may be) at the ladinge of either of the shipps & all the other hatches lockt vpp & that the mr or one of his mate: & the Pursar to stand by the open hatches when any goode are shott into hould, lockinge the same Vpp when they haue left worke, the key to be geven to the Generall or Capteine to be kept.

To buie what is good & not to ourwett any of the Comodities 32

Item to be carefull that nothinge be bought but what is especiall good, & that you doe not ourwett the Cloues when they be laden, for ourwett Cloues bad Nutmegge & Mace haue heretofore beene a greate hindrance vnto vs & taught vs to advise you to be more carefull.

To admitt noe priuate [trade] to any in any of theis Comodities vpon penaltie to loose the same 33.

Item for that voyadges of this Condic̃on & greate chardge cannot admitt any priuate trade or will is that neither you the Generall nor any other vpon any pticular, or other Accompt, then the Generall and iointe stocke doe lade or deale wth any of those Comodities herevnder expressed Viz Pepp, Cloues, Nutmegge, Mace, Synamon, Gynger, Indico, Callicoes, Amber greece, Muske, Alloes, Beniamyn, and Gumlacre. And that yf any shall soe doe the same to be applied to the Accompt of the Companie as our propper goode it beinge noe way reasonable that we should paie them their wage wth meate and drinke, & they lade those thinge in or shipps wch should defray or chardge.

To compare their weightes & measures wth ors before you buie. 34.

Item in eury place where you come and trade Compare their weighte & measures wth ors before you buie, to thend you may knowe the better what to doe & howe to make yor reckoninge for wch purpose we haue put sundrie Cheste wth weighte into or shipps.

Some of the ffactors appointed to weighe what is bought. 35.

Item that there be the sufficientest and best aduiced of or ffactors appointed to weighe what is bought by weight on the land & to keepe a pfect Booke thereof, that the same may be nightlie conferred wth the Pursars Booke, whereby errors may be the better found out.

To bringe some of the Dollors the Hollenders carrie thither. 36.

Item that or ffactors bringe or send by the first shipps 8 or 10 of the Dollers or Royalls wch the Hollenders carrie thither.

Against excessiue drinkinge and banquettinge. 37.

Item we vtterlie forbidd any excessiue drinkeing feastinge or banquetinge abourd the shipps at Sea, or on land it being a greate wast & Consumpc̃on of victualls and wyne, the cause of many diseases & disorders in the Companie, & therefore the same to be spent wth more discrec̃on and sparinge.

To matt the shipps 38.

Item remember to matt the inside of the shipps before you put any spice vnto1 them especiallie where you lade Cloues Pepp Nutmegge and Mace, & be carefull to make choise of the Nutmegge that they be lardg and sound, & at the lading thereof doe not lyme them too much for that doth burne them,2 & beware you lay the Mace in Canisters in some fitt place by it selfe, that it be not spoyled by the heate of the other spices, takeing good heede to buie that wch is bright & not withered nor red nor darke browne Colored, & such Cloues as shall be free of dust, the wch those people vse to putt amongest them for their advantage in the weight.

To sprinkle the Cloues wth water if need be 39.

Item yf necessitie drawe you at the ladinge of the Cloues for better setlinge of them to cast water vpon them, be suer that it be but sprinklinge wth some thinge for the purpose, like a wateringe pott for that too much wett in or Cloues the last voyadge brought vs greate damadge.

To settle afactorie & where if need be & where Comodities are sould better cheepe for gould then for money &c: 40.

Item that if it be thought meete that a ffactorie be setled at Banda, Tornato or Tedore the better to advise the Companie for trade as was formrlie thought fitt in the Comission geven to mr Kealinge & mr Hawkins in the last Voyadge3 you may leaue some to that purpose wth some small stocke if vpon due considerac̃on thereof at yor being there, it shall be soe thought fitt. And seeing that by former Accompte it appeth that those of Luntor and Nere did sell their Cloues & Mace much better cheepe, to receiue their paymt in gould, then in Royalls namelie the Bahare of Nutmegge for 9 Royalls & the Bahare of Mace for 90 Royalls in sylver: But payinge wth gould the Price of Nutmegge but 7 Royalls & of Mace but 70. We therefore thinke it needfull that all meanes be vsed to sell or Comodities for Barter or gould & to finde out such place where gould may be had as especiallie as we are informed at the Iland of ☞ Nouaginnye1 or ells where.

To giue the ffactors chardge often of what they are to obserue by this Comission. 41.
what or ffactors are to procure of the Cheneses &c: 42.

Item that the Generall & Captaines geue often notice to the ffactors & others what they are to obserue by this or Comission wth espetiall chardge to the ffactors to make diligent inquirie of what Comodities are to be bought or bartered for in each Iland, & what English mrchandize may be there vented, & of what kinde and Colors most vendable Item it is to be remembred that or ffactors at Bantam doe their best endevors to pcure the Cheneses to bring from Cheney sleaue and sowing silke of the Color and Syces2 we haue now deliured to you the Generall as alsoe some rawe silke that we may fall into some trade wth them & see yf they can sell any of or English Cloth to them, that they may be brought to thuse thereof.

An Invoice. 43

Item for the quantities of money & mrchandize put into each shipp we referr you to or Invoice deliured you herewth, wth the pticuler sorte Coullors & prices wth paterns of all sorte whereby to make sale as is formrlie made menc̃on of in the 17th Article.

noe voluntarie men or other to goe but such as shall be allowed by the Companie. 44.

Item whereas heretofore the Companie haue receiued greate wronge by the Genrall & Captaines, mrs & Mariners admittance of voluntarie men, to goe in or shipps, we hereby giue an espetiall chardge vnto you or Generall Captaines & mrs: that you suffer none such to goe alonge wth you wch put the Companie to chardge beside many other Inconvenience, nor any but such as shall be allowed of by or direction & whose names are entred into or Booke.

The placeing or
leaueinge of the ffactors at the discrecon of the Genrall & what the are to doe being left. 45.

And yf you shall see cause to leaue any of or ffactors there we doe hereby order that the appointmt of them to recide in those places shall be at the direcc̃on and discrec̃on of you the Generall wherein we hope You will haue that Considerac̃on as to make choise of the fittest wch shall be found able and meete to deserue that trust of ymployment neither lett or placeing them in the seurall shipps as they are placed be any rule to you or any ground to them, to inioye those places of ymploymt, otherwise then they shall be found fitt and deserue, and or further order is that you giue espetiall chardge to such as shall be by you left there to carrie themselues verie kindlie wth those People, for that the Contrarie as we are informed hath beene hurtfull vnto vs, & that some of or mens vnktnde & churlish dealinge towarde them did formrlie make many of those People refraine to deale wth vs, & goe to the Hollenders. And or desier is that such as shall be left there doe there best endevors to finde out trade at Mesopotania1 in the pte of Bengalla Cheremendall St Thome or any other places fitt for trade. And to take good obseruac̃on what English Comodities as Iron, Leade, Tynn, steele, Clothes, kersies, and saies wth their seurall kinde and Colors are there best in request & their values: As alsoe what Comodities are there to be bought as namelie Pintadoes & such like for the Molloccos & likewise Booke Calicutte and Lawnes called Casa and such other thinge as may serue for England, where the first sorte will serue best wth Pearles, stoanes Muske Bezar, and such like wth their seurall prices, wherein we wish or men to be ymployed, each man accordinge to his skill, the omission for seekeing out whereof all this while hath retourned to or greate losse, and to the benefitt of the Hollenders whoe haue beene laborious and industrious therein, & this inquirie to be made yf it be possible before yor retourne to thend that at yor retourne to England we may be effectuallie adurticed of all theis pticulars soe far as you may, & of all other thinge for or better direcc̃ons in the next voyadge.

Not to ymparte the trade to any but the Company 46.

Item for that it is vnfitt & inconvenient that or trade be ympted vnto any but or genrall Companie it is expreslie ordered, & soe the ffactors are to haue chardge not to write or aduice any their pticuler freinde or others of the prices of any Comodities, either bought or sould But onelie in their genrall łres to the Gournor and Companie.

To bring an Inventory of goodes debtes and moneys you shall leaue in those partes 47

Item that you or Generall at yor retourne from those pte for England doe bringe wth you vnto vs from thence an Inventorie of all or goode debte & moneys wch you then shall happen to leaue remaineing in any those pte puttinge to this or genrall Accompte all guifte presente and gratifica~õns wch shall be geven by any forreine Prince or Potentate vnto whome we haue now sent Presente or others.

To giue to the Admirall at Bantam a Present (if need be) 48

And further or direc~õn is that you or Generall att yor comeing to Bantam doe beside the łre and present to that kinge giue vnto the Admirall & such other greate psonadge theare as or ffactors shall aduise you to haue beene freindlie to them, such present or gratifica~õn as shall be thought fitt, and by their further kinde dealeinge wth you they shall deserue.

A ffactorie at Priamon (if it may be). 49
To bring some Tynn from Bantam &c: 50

And alsoe yf Convenientlie you may we wish that a ffactorie or at least some of or people be appointed to recide at Priamon both for their better health and saffetie, & for pcuring for vs pepp & other Comodities: yf there shall be men and stocke there to ymploie & you shall see iuste cause to doe the same Item or direc~õn is that at yor retourne from Bantam you doe bringe thence for the Companie some small quantitie of the East India Tynn for triall & proofe thereof.

What is to be done aboute the ffact of Sr Edward Michelborne (if need be) 51.

Item Touching the ffacte Comitted by Sr Edward Michelborne1 though we and the rest of or Companie knowe or selues to be meerelie innocent therein, Yet if by any meanes we or or goode should be dampnified thereby we wish you soe farr as saffelie you may to seeke to that Kinge and Magistrate for redresse and recompence thereof. The wch yf you cannot obtaine then or will is that you vse the benefitt geuen you in that behalfe, soe farr forth as you shall see cause & be free of further danger.

To buie of the lardgest pepper. 52

And for that we finde best proffitt by the lardge sorte of Pepp both for the price that you pay aswell for thone as for theother, we pray you at any hand to buie soe much of the lardgest sorte as by any meanes you can gett, and let the same be put by it selfe into the shipp that it be not mingled wth any other.

53.

Item after the depture of the said Alexander Sharpie and Richard Rowles to diurs Coaste as thone for England & thother as we haue by this Comission ordered yf the said Richard Rowles shall happen to die (wch god forbidd) then we doe appointe in his place for ordering and effectinge the busines by vs hereby Comitted vnto the said Richard Rowles his chardge vnto Richard Reaue ffactor, But neurthelesse if the said Richard Rowles shall happen to die before he shall pte Companie wth the said Alexander Sharpie for diurs place as aforesaid, Then or expresse will is that Willm Revett1 factor be appointed in the place of the said Richard Rowles of Leiuetenant Generall in this present voyadge before any other. As alsoe by the death of the said Alexander Sharpie now or Generall to succeede his place and chardge in the absence of the said Richard Rowles by death or otherwise vntill their meeteinge together againe in this voyadge.

54.

Item now lastlie & wthe the first to be remembred we Comend vnto you all an espetiall care to haue yor Eyes open to all deuices & practises wch may be wrought against you or shipps and goode in eury place where you come keepinge a continuall watch, whereby you may be readie to prevent any mischeefe intended against you suspect all howe freindlie soeur they seeme to be be redie still and stand vpon yor guarde truste not yor saffetie to the carelesse attendance of the Comon Mariners whoe will not loose their present pleasures or ease though the losse of yor liues or shipps and goode depend vpon it. And albeit we haue sett downe eury thinge what we remember & desier to be done in pticular, Yet yf vpon due Consideracõn you finde cause to aulter any thinge, wch we heare haue sett downe, haueing wth good aduice resolued therevpon we referr the same to yor discrec̃ons, & for yor better assistance & warie proceedinges therein as alsoe in all other or affaires we appointe Will̃m Revett Richard Reaue and Iohn Iourdan, if you see noe cause to the Contrarie & such others as you the principall Comanders shall thinke fitt to Consider and Consult wth you the Generall of all thinge needfull, whome we wish you to imbrace & vse wth a loueinge respect & freindlie & diligentlie to hearken to their Councells puttinge in execuc̃on what shall wth good deliberac̃on be soe agreed vpon: And soe we Comend you and yor endevors to Gode prouidence whoe guide you wth his feare & defend you from all dangers. Amen.

Thinge deliured by the Companie to mr Alexander Sharpie Generall in March 1607. Viz.

1. Nprimis This Comission of the Companie vnder their seale signed by the Secretarie.

2. Item 12 l̃res from his matie: & the English of them to Prince in the Indies.1

3. Item a saffe Conduct from his matie: vnder the priuie seale for passadge of or men from the Indies ourland wth a Coppie thereof in English.2

4. Item a Comission to mr Sharpie Genrall & a duplicate to mr Richard Rowles Leiuetenant Genrall vnder the greate seale of England, the wch duplicatt is to remaine in his hande vntill they twoe depte Companie.3

5. Item a Coppie of the Priviledge obtayned by Sr Iames Lancaster at Dachem & Sumatra to the Companie4 his obseruac̃on of tymes meete to be obserued in the East Indies5 And the Discripc̃on of the Ilande of Banda Amboyna Selebes or Makasser Botton Seran wth the wares therein spent and bought & their weighte together wth crteine direcc̃ons for saileing vpon the Coaste in the Indies.1

6. A lre howe to deale wth Salbancke according to order of Courte the 5th of March 1607.2

7. An order of Courte held the 11th of the said monneth of March, not to deale in any other mannr but by way of honest mrchandize3

8. A lre to the ffactors of the 3 voyadge4 wth a Coppie thereof & of theirs formrlie sent the last yeare for better vnderstandinge what is to be pformed on their pte of the 4th voyadg wth a note of the manner of his priuate trade & howe the same is to be registred &c:

9. An Invoice of all moneys & other thinge now sent: Carracters5 to write Overland (if need be) & Beames weighte & Scales &c.

Thinge then deliured to mr Richard Rowles Leiuetenante genrall.

I. Inprimis the foresaid Comission of the Companie vnder their seale signed by the Secretory

2 A Coppie of the foresaid Priuiledge obtayned by Sr Iames Lancaster at Dachem wth the obseruac̃on of tymes in the Indies & the discripc̃on of Ilande wares weighte & direcc̃on for saileinge vpon the Coaste of the Indies &c: before mencioned.

3 An other lre to the ffactors of the 3 voyadge for the more saffetie in deliury thereof accordinge to the supscripc̃on wth a note of the mannr of his priuate trade & how the same is to be registred &c: The Copies of all thinge before mencioned are formrlie recorded in this Register.

THE some of a Passe1 to be procured for the East India Companie from the Grandsignior to A B and C D Gournors of his Citties of Aden and Mocca at the mouth of the red sea & to all & eury other his Officers Gournors and superiors of any his Provinces Citties Townes Seas Rivers & Bridge &c: thereaboute, or ells where in any his Dominions.

The some of a saffe Conducte from the Grand signior.

That whereas he and his Predicessors are and haue beene for the space of many yeares in league and amitie wth the mightie kinge of England & the subiecte of that kingdome haue longe had and now haue free traffique and trade in Marchandizeing in his dominions and Countries through the Mediterranean Seas: And whereas some of the Subiecte of that kingdome (as he is informed[]) haueing wth their greate chardge and labor found out atrade in Theast Indies, & heareing of the fame & wealth of some pte of his Countries in their passadge to the said Indies, are desirous to vizitt those place for thenlardginge of their said trade. And Considering how beneficiall the same may be to him & his kingdomes, & that such men in soe good an enterprize proffitable to humane Societie deserue not onelie praise and favor but alsoe aide and helpe soe far as may be lawfullie & convenientlie yealded. He hath beene pleased of his Princelie favor to vouchsaffe them theis his łres of saffe Conducte and Comendačon Comanding the said A B. and C D. and all other his said Officers &c: not onelie kindlie and loueinglie to enterteine and receiue the said Marchaunte subiecte of England, comeing or passinge throughe, or by any of his dominions assistinge and releiueinge them wth all thinge needfull for them selues, their men and shipps: But alsoe freelie to pmitt them by land or by Sea to goe or saile to goe forward, or retourne and as their occasion shall requier to remaine in any his Countries Citties or dominions, grantinge them such libtie of traffique and priuiledge as shall be reasonable, wthout giueing or sufferinge any lett hindrance Iniurie or molestačon to be offered or done vnto them, & yealdinge vnto them such offices of benevolence & humanitie as shall be convenient to be yealded honest men and strangers vndertakeinge soe longe and laborious a iourney handlinge their owne affaires & behaueing them selues honestlie and peaceablie.

To or verie loueing freind mr Hum: Smyth mrchant at Hull.

AFTER1 or hartie Comendačóns &c: fforasmuch as we haue an intent to buie the shipp at Hull called the mrchaunt Royall soe as shee vpon veiwe may be found fitting for vs in all respectę aswell in her price as goodnes: & vnderstanding that by some yor affaires, you now haue occasion to be at Hull or thereaboutę: we haue thought yt good and haue soe concluded to send the bearer hereof mr Robert Earle vnto you a man skilfull in shippinge to thend that by or instrucčóns giuen him (a coppie whereof we send you here inclosed) & yor good direcčóns, a diligent veiwe and inquirie may be taken of her, both for her price, goodnes, strength, breadth and fitnes for or seruice, as for or saffe inioyinge of her &c: Wherefore we pray you to make ymployment of the said mr Earle herein, & to giue him yor helping hand for the pformance thereof in the best manner you may for the good of the Company. And further we doe requier you (yf you wth the advice of the said mr Earle) shall soe finde the said shipp in all respectę as aforesaid fitt for or service to vse the best meanes you cann to buie her for thuse of this Companie soe as you may haue her deliured here at London wth all thingę now belonging vnto her vnder or for the some of seaven hundred poundę at the most for the cheeffest man of abilitie and otherwise wth whome you are to deale for sale and securitie of her we conceiue to be mr Ioseph ffeild a man not vnknowne vnto you as we vnderstand But yf you cann not bargaine for her vnder or at that price at the most then we pray you to crtifie vs of the pticulars thereof by the said mr Earle or by some more speedie Messenger that vpon receipt of yor łres we may resolue what to doe in the same. And thus not doubting of yor care and kindnes we comitt you to the tuicõn of Thalmightie London the 20th of Aprill 1608.

Yor loueing freinde the Adventurers of theast India Company in the 4th voyadge.

The Twenteth of Aprill 1608.

A remembraunce for mr Robert Earle to be sent to Hull about veiwing of the shipp there to be sould called the mrchant Royall.1

INPRIMIS you are wthall convenient expedicõn to goe for Kingston vpon Hull or to Beverley or theareaboute to mr Humfrey Smyth of London mrchaunt at what place you may there first finde him & deliuring him theis or łres you are to take and ffollowe what direccõns he shall giue you in this busines.

Item you comeinge thither and findinge (wth the advice of the said mr Smyth) that the said shipp may be for or seruice, you are to make diligent search and veiwe of her, of what strength she is of, what crosse beames, futtick Riders,2 bottume riders & needfull stannders3 &c: she hath in her: whereby yt may be the better conceiued what the cost will be to make her fitt for or voyadge.

Item you are crteinelie to learne her burthen, her breadth her length: how much water she draweth in her ballast, & howe much full laden, yf she be any way weakened by the longe lyinge not ymployed: her adge, & yf all her tymbers be sounde.

Item you are to vnderstand & see howe she is fitted wth good maste, sailes, yarde, Cables & other furniture.

Item you are to make inquirie howe she is Condicioned in her saileing & steridge as otherwise: & alsoe what ordinance she hath, of weight and length &c: & of all other thinge needfull.

Item to learne her lowest price, & in that price what ordinance maste sailes yarde Cables & other thinge are to be sould wth her and being bought howe she may be brought hither & at whose chardge & what good securitie may be had for enioyinge of her, & by whome yt will be geven.

Lastlie you are to make an Inventorie of all the premisses in writeinge the better to informe vs at yor retourne, in what state she is, what she hath & what she wanteth & the same being pformed you are to retourne by the first meanes you may: But yf before yor comeing thither yt shall fall out that mr Humfrey Smyth shall be retourned thence for London then you are to followe theis yor direccons wthout him wherein you are to vse all care & expedicon & Retourne.

A Bill of Adventure to mr. Groues
this is corrected & 2 made as it was deliured to his wieff

HEAREAS1 we the Gournor and Company of Marchaunte of London trading into the East Indies Haue interteyned and hired Phillipp de Graeffe of the precinct of St Katherines neare to Tower of London Mariner to goe as principall mr in one of the twoe shipps now latelie by vs prepared & sent in or fourth voyadge for those pte. And haue allowed and paied him for his ymployment in the said voyadge before his depture hence theis seurall somes following Viz. The some of One hundred Twentie and ffyve pounde for his prepacon to sea: The some of Twentie pounde for fower monnethes Harborrow wage after the rate of ffyve pounde p̃ monneth: The some of ffortie shillinge for Boate hier: And further vpon his intreatie haue lent and ymprested vnto him the some of Eeighteene pounde ouʳ & aboue the somes formerlie giuen him, the wᶜʰ some of Eighteene pounde is onelie to be defalked out of such proffitt of Adventure as hereafter is granted him. Now knowe yee that we the said Gouʳnoʳ & Company, for further allowance & recompence of the good service travell and paines wᶜʰ he the said Phillipp de Graeffe faithfullie p̃myseth to to his best endeuoʳˢ to p̃forme in the said voyadge both outwarde & homewarde for the good of the said Company Doe by theis presente for vs & oʳ Successoʳˢ promyse and agree to giue and allowe vnto him the said Phillipp de Graeffe his Executoʳˢ Administratoʳˢ or Assignes, vpon the gaine & proffitt wᶜʰ god shall send by the retourne of the same voyadge (the principall Adventure thereof, & all chardge of the voyadge goode & mʳchandizes of what kinde soeuʳ both by land or water first borne & deducted[])] Soe much gaine as ffyve hundred and fyftie pounde will produce that is to saie such rate & pffitt as yf he had beene an Adventurer of the some of ffyve hundred and ffyftie pounde, & as yf he had put in soe much readie money in stocke in the said voyadge. The wᶜʰ rate and proporc̃on of proffitt is to be paid vnto him the said Phillip de Graeff his Executoʳˢ Adˢ or Assignes in such manner and forme · as the gaine and proffitt of the said voyadge shall be paid to all other the Adventurers genʳallie, vpon the some of ffyue hundred and ffyftie pounde by them adventured.

But if he happen to die before the retourne of the said shipps from the said East Indies, or those other place whither they they are directed, hauinge liued & Contynued in the said voiadge vntill the shipps, or shipp wherein he shall serue shall arriue & come to such porte in those parte, at wᶜʰ it shalbe founde fitt to lade the same: Then the said gaine p̃porcioned of the said rate of 550li aduenture to be paid to his Executoʳˢ Adˢ or Assignes, as it should haue been paid vnto him, if he had retourned wᵗʰ the said shipps. Prouided alwaies that if [he] decease before the shipps shall arriue to such porte in those pte at wᶜʰ they are to take in their ladinge. That then the moneys imprested & deliuʳed him before his goinge to Sea shalbe vnto him, in full recompence of his entertainemt formerlie agreed vppon for the voiadge. And vppon theis Condicõns & pviso before menc̃oed we the Gournor & Companie vnder or Comon Seale, haue giuen vnto the said Phillip de Graeff this p̄nte Bill of Contract & aduenture dated the 20th day of Iune 1608 And in the yeare of the reigne of or soureigne lord Iames Kinge of England ffrance & Ireland the Sixt & of Scotland the one & fforteth.

The Bill of an Aduenturer of 550li, in the 4th voiadge, to an Adventurer vnder him

Wheareas Wiłłm Iennyngꬵ Citizen and of London one of the Adventurers and one of the Brethren of the Company of Marchauntꬵ of London trading into the East Indies Hath not onelie Adventured the some of 100li vnder me Wiłłm Bonham Citizen and Vintener of London & alsoe one of the Adventurers & one of the said Company of mrchantꬵ tradinge into the East Indies in their fourth voyadge for those p̄tꬵ: But hath likewyse trulie paid the said some of 100li to me the said William Bonham as appeth by the register of the said Company the 4th of March 1607.1 Now knowe yee that I the said Wiłłm Bonham doe by theis p̄ntꬵ p̄myse and agree to & wth the said Wiłłm Iennyngꬵ That I the said Wiłłm Bonham my Executorrs & Administratorrs shall & will vpon the retourne of the shipps or either of them sett out by the said Company in their said 4th voyadge or wthin Convenient tyme after their said retourne in the same deliur vnto the said Wiłłm Iennyngꬵ his Executorrs Administratorrs or Assignes a true and iust accompt and paymt of the said some of 100li soe by him adventured vnder me & of the proffitt & benefitt wch god shall send thereof ratablelie and accordinge to the genrall distribucõn proporcõn and allotmt wch shall be allotted disposed and geven to me the said Wiłłm Bonham & to all other the seurall Adventurers of 550li in the said fourth voyadge proporcionallie to each mans seurall Adventure. In witnes whereof I haue herevnto sett my hand and seale the 4th day of Iulie 1608. And in the Yeare of the Reign of &c:

The Bill of Adventure of 550li in the fourth voyadge to an Adventurer vnder him the Bill on totherside of this leafe1 not being allowed.
